MINUTES
  MALIBU PLANNING COMMISSION
  REGULAR MEETING
  SEPTEMBER 6, 2022
  TELECONFERENCED VARIOUS LOCATIONS
  -

  6:30 P.M.

The following meeting was held pursuant to the Governor’s Executive Orders N-25-20
and N-29-20 and fully teleconferenced from various locations during the coronavirus
disease (COVID-19) pandemic.

CALL TO ORDER

  Chair Hill called the meeting to order at 6:30 p.m.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Chair Kraig Hill, Vice Chair Dennis Robert Smith, and Commissioners Jeffrey
  Jennings, John Mazza, and Mark Wetton

  ALSO PRESENT: Patrick Donegan, Assistant City Attomey; Richard Mollica, Planning
  Director; Adrian Fernandez, Assistant Planning Director; Jessica Thompson, Senior
  Planner; Tyler Eaton, Associate Planner; Adam Pisarkiewicz, Contract Planner; Fletcher
  Allen, Planning Technician; Courtney McCarnmon, City Biologist~~, Lauren Doyel,
  Contract Geotechnical Engineer; and Rebecca Evans. Recording Secretary

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

MOTION  Commissioner Mazza moved and Commissioner Jennings seconded a motion to
  approve the agenda as recommended by staff and to continue Item No. 5.C. to
  September 19, 2022.

  The question was called and the motion carried unanimously.

REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  Recording Secretary Evans reported that the agenda for the meeting was properly posted
  on August 26, 2022.

ITEM 1  CEREMONIAL/PRESENTATIONS
  A. Planning Commission Reorganization
   Malibu Planning Commission
  Minutes of September 6, 2022
  Page 2 of 12

MOTION  Chair Hill moved and Commissioner Jennings seconded a motion for the Planning
  Commission to continue to vote for Chair and Vice Chair positions until candidates
  for each position achieved a majority vote.

  The question was called and the motion carried unanimously.

  1. Election of Chair

MOTION  Chair Hill moved and Commissioner Mazza seconded a motion to nominate Chair
  Hill to continue to serve as Chair of the Planning Commission until after incoming
  City Councilmembers appointed new Planning Commissioners in January 2023.

MOTION  Commissioner Mazza moved and Chair I-jill seconded a motion nominating
  Commissioner Wetton to serve as Chair of the Planning Commission.

MOTION  Commissioner Jennings moved and Commissioner Wetton seconded a motion
  nominating Vice Chair Smith to serve as Chair of the Planning Commission.

  The question was called and Commissioners Jennings, Wetton and Smith voted for
  Vice Chair Smith to serve as Chair of the Planning Commission; Commissioner
  Mazza voted for Commissioner Wetton to serve as Chair of the Planning
  Commission; and Chair Hill voted for himself to serve as Chair of the Planning
  Commission. Vice Chair Smith was elected as Chair olthe Planning Commission
  3-2.

  2. Election of Vice Chair

MOTION  Commissioner Jennings moved and Commissioner Hill seconded a motion to
  nominate Commissioner Mazza to serve as Vice Chair of the Planning
  Commission.

  The question was called and Commissioners Jennings, Mazza, Wetton and Chair
  Smith voted for Commissioner Mazza to serve as Vice Chair of the Planning
  Commission, and Commissioner Hill voted for Commissioner Wetton to serve as
  Vice Chair of the Planning Commission. Commissioner Mazza was elected as Vice
  Chair of the Planning Commission, 4-I.

  Recording Secretary Evans administered the Oath of Office to Chair Smith and
  Vice Chair Mazza.

ITEM 2.A.  PUBLIC COMMENTS
  None.

ITEM 2.B.  COMMISSION I STAFF COMMENTS

  Vice Chair Mazza asked for clarification on why an appeal on the September 1 2,
  2022 City Council agenda (18868 Pacific Coast Highway / Coastal Development
  Permit No. 1 7-075), appeared to have been based on a revised version of the
  application presented to the Planning Commission.

  Planning Director Mollica clarified that during the time between the Planning
  Commission’s denial and the appeal to City Council, the applicant offered to move
  the home back an additional eight to ten feet. He stated that he had explained to the
  applicant that their option was to appeal the project as previously presented to the
  Planning Commission or to return to the Planning Commission with a new
  application, which could include the offer to revise plans by moving the residence
  back further. He further stated the staff report prepared for the City Council meeting
  was based on the project denied by the Planning Commission and the City Council
  has a few different options, as outlined in the agenda report.

  Vice Chair Mazza expressed concern that language in the report implied an
  argument for a new project, which would be a bad precedent for Malibu.

  Commissioner Hill agreed with much of what Vice Chair Mazza stated. However,
  he noted that the City Council’s role is de novo.

  Planning Director Mollica added that applicants have a right to comment as they
  see fit. The analysis by staff was focused on the proJect the Planning Commission
  denied. An option to remand the project back to the Planning Commission was
  included for City Council consideration.

  Commissioner Jennings noted that past practice frowned on Planning
  Commissioners’ testimony to the City Council regarding how to interpret the
  Planning Commission’s action.

  Commissioner Wetton requested an update on live music at Trancas Canyon
  Market on Friday nights and asked if a Temporary Use Permit could cover a series
  of events with one per weekend.

  In response to Commissioner Wetton, Planning Director Mollica stated that there
  is a pending Conditional Use Permit application for the Trancas Canyon Market.
  Code Enforcement have issued a citation for past events due to evidence of advance
  advertising. Trancas Canyon Market did apply for a Temporary Use Permit for the
  events planned for the end of September. However, based on recent conversations,
  Trancas Canyon Market may choose not to complete the Temporary Use Permit
  process and instead reduce the scope of events. Planning Director Mollica noted
   Malibu Planning Commission
  Minutes of September 6, 2022
  Page 4 of 12

 that the Planning Department will bring a Temporary Use Permit discussion back
 to the Zoning Ordinance Revisions and Code Enforcement Subcommittee in the
 near future, in part to address issues including nonconsecutive series of events.

Planning Director Mollica reported that potential planning consultants have been
interviewed and job openings for Assistant and Associate Planner positions were
posted. He also provided an update on the new online application portal, intended
to streamline the submittal process. Documents can be sent digitally, and applicants
will not need to drive to City Hall to begin the application process.

Chair Smith stated that he attended and enjoyed the Chili Cook Off on Friday night.
He asked for an update on why there were stakes in the ground on the former Malibu
Bay Company land near Trancas Canyon Road and Pacific Coast Highway.

In response to Chair Smith, Assistant Planning Director Fernandez noted that there
is an application for a four-lot subdivision and a parcel map for a larger lot
purchased. The applicant has been conducting geotesting for future development of
those four lots.

Chair Smith requested an update on the status of the Malibu Inn Motel project.

In response to Chair Smith, Planning Director Mollica remarked the Conditional
Use Permit Amendment approved by the Planning Commission was appealed to
the City Council and will be heard on October 10, 2022. If the appeals are denied,
the Recording Secretary will poll Commissioners on availability for a Special
Planning Commission meeting in November to consider the Malibu Inn Motel
proj ect.

Chair Smith suggested a Planning Department staff member visit the I 8868 Pacific
Coast Highway site. He was appalled by the appeal filed against 31113 Bailard
Avenue.

Vice Chair Mazza asked Planning Director Mollica why the department was hiring
at the Assistant and Associate levels at this time and whether it was a change from
the 3-year plan presented to City Council. 1-le further asked if there was a plan to
hire Code Enforcement Officers to enforce the Dark Sky Ordinance in the evening.

In response to Vice Chair Mazza, Planning Director Mollica clarified that the
Assistant and Associate Planner openings were intended to fill current vacancies in
the Planning Department. 1-le recently made an offer to a Code Enforcement Officer
candidate with twenty years of experience. Planning Director Mollica planned to
locate a candidate with an engineering/plan check background to work within Code
Enforcement on Dark Sky Ordinance issues. When the new compliance officer has
   Malibu Planning Commission
  Minutes of September 6,2022
  Page 5 of 12

  been trained, the goal is to test 7-day per week code compliance in the City with
  four 1 0-hour shifts per employee.

  Vice Chair Mazza requested updates on the status of Hotel June obtaining a
  Conditional Use Permit and Coastal Development Permit and the former Beau
  Rivage’s stalled Conditional Use Permit application.

  In response to Vice Chair Mazza, Planning Director Mollica offered to provide an
  updated report in the future but based on his recollection, both projects received
  incomplete letters and required additional items. The former Beau Rivage property
  (26025 Pacific Coast Highway) appeared to be changing course to a smaller project.
  Hotel June was not serving alcohol based on code enforcement investigation and
  have not acted on the items in their Conditional Use Permit application.
